title: Moving averages
summary: A moving average smooths recent closes into one line. Its slope summarises direction, and it always lags price.
unreliableWhen: In sideways markets, price crosses a flat average again and again, so crossover rules flip back and forth. After sharp turns, the average reacts late.
goodExample: Price stays above a rising EMA 50 through a trend, with the SMA 20 above it.
badExample: Buying every time price crosses above the SMA 20 in a sideways market, and paying costs on each flip.

chart.lookFor: Watch the slope of both averages and how far behind price they turn. Then open Sideways and count how often price crosses the SMA 20.
